detailed_rationale:
IndiaMART InterMESH runs India's largest B2B marketplace/directory, monetizing via paid supplier subscriptions for enhanced listings and lead generation. The balance sheet remains a fortress (D/E ~0.01x, interest coverage ~158x - effectively debt-free with a large cash/investment surplus), and headline FY26 revenue grew 13% to Rs 1,569 crore. But underneath that, FY26 was a genuinely weak year on the metrics that matter most for a subscription platform: paying suppliers fell by a net 1,200 in Q4 to 220K - the platform's first-ever decline in paying subscribers since COVID - and paid-subscriber growth has decelerated from 15-18% in FY23-24 to just 8-10% in FY26 as management itself now describes the addressable pool of willing-to-pay SME sellers as saturating. Unique business enquiries fell in the most recent quarter, and collections growth (the best proxy for forward revenue) slowed to single digits.

Profitability tells the same story, and this is not just a one-off quarter: full-year FY26 net profit fell 13% to Rs 474.7 crore (from Rs 550.7 crore in FY25) despite revenue growing 13% - i.e., operating leverage ran in reverse for the full year, not merely in one bad print. Q4 FY26 alone saw net profit crash 72.2% YoY to Rs 50.2 crore (from Rs 180.6 crore), driven by a mix of a small one-off (Rs 9.07 crore new-labour-code provision), a Rs 33.9 crore loss in the 'other income' line (consistent with mark-to-market losses on the company's treasury/startup investment book, a non-operating item that could reverse), and genuinely higher operating expenses (total expenses up 19% YoY, outpacing 14% revenue growth) - so part of the Q4 collapse is noise, but the full-year margin compression is real and not explained away by any single item.

The most important qualitative finding is a live structural risk: IndiaMART has publicly complained after its own website was excluded from ChatGPT's listing/search results, an unusually direct, company-acknowledged signal that AI-powered search and sourcing tools bypassing traditional B2B directories is now a real threat to the business model, not a theoretical one - and management itself could not quantify on the earnings call how much of the enquiry decline is LLM-related traffic diversion versus other causes. Sell-side coverage is genuinely split on this: Nomura (Reduce, target Rs 1,900) and Nuvama (target Rs 1,970) have turned cautious, while JM Financial upgraded to Buy citing medium-term positives - this is a real, unresolved debate among professional analysts, not a settled call.
recommendation_rationale: Quant scores this Hold on both windows, but the 1-year composite (45.4) is materially weaker than the 3-year (54.0), reflecting the real-time deceleration - and my own research finds enough substance behind that gap (first-ever subscriber decline since COVID, a full-year profit decline despite revenue growth, and a company-acknowledged AI-disruption risk) that I am flagging this rather than passing it through silently. I am not overriding to Sell - I cannot, and more importantly the balance sheet and brand moat are real assets that argue against a clean Sell call - but I believe this is a genuine Hold-vs-Sell judgment call for the desk rather than a comfortable Hold.
summary: IndiaMART remains debt-free and highly cash-generative, but the business is showing its first real cracks: paying-subscriber numbers fell for the first time since COVID, subscriber and enquiry growth have both slowed sharply, and full-year profit actually declined even as revenue grew - a sign that costs are now outrunning growth, not a one-quarter blip. Layered on top is a new and serious risk: AI-powered search tools may increasingly let buyers find suppliers without going through IndiaMART's directory at all, and the company has publicly complained about being excluded from ChatGPT's results. Sell-side analysts are split, with some cutting targets and others staying constructive. We rate this a Hold, but flag it for the desk given the combination of a real growth deceleration and an unresolved structural risk to the core model.
positive_para: Rock-solid balance sheet (near-zero debt, interest coverage ~158x) gives the company years of runway to adapt even if growth slows further; deferred revenue still grew 17% YoY to Rs 1,965 crore, providing some forward revenue visibility; IndiaMART retains by far the largest supplier base and brand recognition among Indian SME sourcing platforms, which is a real moat even if growth has matured; management is at least publicly engaging with the AI-disruption question (the ChatGPT-exclusion complaint) rather than ignoring it; valuation (PE ~24.6x, value_score ~68/100) is no longer the stretched multiple the stock carried in its high-growth years.
negative_para: The core growth engine is genuinely slowing, not just facing a tough comparison: paying suppliers fell in absolute terms for the first time since COVID, subscriber growth has roughly halved (15-18% to 8-10%), and full-year PAT fell 13% even as revenue rose 13% - real operating deleverage, not an isolated bad quarter. The AI/LLM sourcing-disruption risk is no longer hypothetical - the company's own complaint about ChatGPT exclusion is first-hand evidence management is worried about exactly this channel shift, and neither management nor this analyst can yet quantify how large that risk is. Two respected brokerages (Nomura, Nuvama) have already cut ratings/targets on these concerns, and until subscriber and enquiry trends stabilize, the honest read is that the business is past its high-growth phase and now needs to prove it can defend its moat against a structurally different competitive threat.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~24.6x trailing earnings, the market has already de-rated IndiaMART well off its former growth multiple, which is appropriate given subscriber growth has roughly halved and full-year profit just declined. The multiple no longer prices in aggressive growth, but it also does not yet price in a scenario where AI-native sourcing tools materially erode the core directory model - if that risk proves real over the next few years, even today's more modest multiple could prove too rich; if IndiaMART successfully defends its moat (e.g., by embedding itself into the AI-search layer rather than being disintermediated by it), today's price could look like fair value for a maturing cash-compounder. I would call this a genuine, unresolved fork rather than clearly cheap or clearly rich.
escalation_reason: IndiaMART posted its first-ever decline in paying subscribers since COVID and a full-year (not merely one-off-quarter) profit decline despite revenue growth in FY26, alongside a company-acknowledged, first-hand signal (its own complaint over ChatGPT search exclusion) that AI-powered sourcing tools bypassing B2B directories is now a live risk to the core business model. Sell-side coverage is genuinely split (Nomura/Nuvama cautious vs JM Financial constructive). This combination - real structural deceleration plus an unresolved, potentially business-model-level disruption risk - is exactly the kind of Hold-vs-Sell judgment call that should get a direct CIO/PM look rather than a mechanical Hold pass-through.
